incidents.name: FlooringPeriphery extMulticall arbitrary call
incidents.notes: FlooringPeriphery.extMulticall() executed caller-supplied (target, calldata) pairs with no access control or target allowlist, so the attacker made the periphery call safeTransferFrom on NFT collections and pull Pudgy Penguins and other NFTs out of every wallet that had approved it.

sources.ref: onchain review: FlooringPeriphery 0xc538d17a6aacc5271be5f51b891e2e92c8187edd created 2023-12-05T09:09:59Z by 0x43800c438f5d639c8b865396cb83a4efa220091b, unrelated to the attack sender; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (11.7 days). Loss is in NFTs (BAYC, Pudgy Penguins and others), valued at ~$1.6M in the PoC header and contemporaneous reporting; no deep-market unit conversion applies. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): FlooringPeriphery is deployed directly (Etherscan verifies the source at the victim address itself and no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot is set) and its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 18719162 and the incident block 18802289; its two DELEGATECALL sites are both OpenZeppelin Address.functionDelegateCall, reachable only from Multicall - which passes address(this) - and from the UUPS upgradeToAndCall path, which the onlyProxy/__self check makes unreachable on a directly deployed logic contract, so the executing code is the victim's own unchanged runtime.
